touches.text: Install and upgrades live here: the installer machine walks the host-seam intentions, verifies each, offers what's missing, applies, re-verifies. If xyz library needs an update, this is the component that does it. Any change to what the host is goes through here (6.6.3.1.1).

Skills (skills/: cairnhelp, challenge, chart, commit, intent, sorted, ...) are Claude Code's. The deterministic parts move out of markdown into CC device verbs: a skill's OS-side work runs as a script, and CC's shim processes the result and injects it into the session. WHY: every habit captured that way is one CC no longer spends inference on, so CC gets faster; a first charting pass done in deterministic Python with no LLM until after saved about 90% of tokens, measured in real use.
Any cairn command brings up whatever it needs, including the whole install on the very first run (6.3.2). WHY: a well designed tool should disappear in use.

conflicts.text: Machine: tools plus the glue that holds them together. Has an owner. Anything that calls another component, uses other tools, or owns state it must gate is a machine. Lives inside its device (cairn/devices/<device>/machines/<machine>/), or in cairn/machines/ when several devices hold one (16).
conflicts.ticket_says: The installer's code lives at cairn/machines/installer/
conflicts.why: Line 1.3.2 says machines live at cairn/devices/<device>/machines/ if they belong to one device, or cairn/machines/ only when several devices hold one. Line 6.3.5 places the installer in Recovery's section ('Install and upgrades live here'), indicating one owner. By 1.3.2's location rule, Recovery's installer should be at cairn/devices/recovery/machines/installer/, not cairn/machines/installer/ (which is reserved for shared machines per section 16).
